To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a geometrical classification of instructions can be used to identify any sequence of instructions, (2) the proposed approach can be used to reverse the general purpose code execution of a recent secure chip, (3) the proposed approach is able to reverse code execution with a success rate of 100% on a test set of 100 sequences of instructions.

(1) we have shown how to use a simple and effective method based on Syntactic Pattern Matching to reverse general purpose instructions; and (2) we have demonstrated how this method can be used to reverse the instructions of a secure component.
we have developed a new approach for recovering the executed code of embedded systems based on the analysis of the power consumption.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reverse engineering of the code executed by the secure components, using a pattern recognition approach.
the development of a methodology for reverse engineering embedded software using power consumption analysis.
the reverse engineering of embedded software through power consumption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this approach is a very promising technique to recover the code executed in a secure component.
the approach presented in this paper can be used to improve the power consumption analysis of embedded systems.
our method is able to recover the executed instructions with an error rate of 0.3% on average and a maximum error rate of 3.6%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to propose a pattern recognition approach to recover the code executed by a secure device.
the presented method allows the automatic identification of the instructions executed in a secure component, and therefore the recovery of the code itself.
the presented method is able to recover the executed instruction sequence from a given power consumption trace, without any knowledge of the executed program or its execution context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pattern recognition methodology is a powerful and generic approach for the reverse engineering of embedded software using power consumption analysis.
the proposed method can be used in an automated manner to reverse the code of a secure component and that the obtained information can be used to improve the SPA.
the proposed method can be used to identify the instructions that leak through the power consumption, which can help to improve other attacks.
